title: First Ellington sessions, 1930
summary: Dance lists the 1930 sessions: Rent Party Blues, Jungle Blues, Ring Dem Bells, The Mooch, where Cootie used the plunger.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah, that's right. That's right. Well, let me see. Just let me check this and make sure this is going all right.
Yeah.

Well, Cootie, I think it might not be a bad idea if we started talking about some of those records that were made, from the time that you first went with the band. For instance, in January 1930, I guess that was the first session you made with the band. I'll tell you what titles were on that. "Rent Party Blues" was on it, and "Jungle Blues". And "St. James Infirmary". There was a fourth number, but I don't think I have that down. But that was the first session that you made with them. "Jungle Blues" I guess you were perhaps using the plunger. Do you recall that at all?
No. I don't recall that.
I mean, that's only oh, going to be a
blues.
Yeah.

I don't think it was ever remade or anything. But anyway, it was first. But in April in 1930, that was a very good session. And incidentally, Tizol Teazle came in the band in '29. Last time, when you and I talked about it, I thought Teazle came quite a bit later than that, but he must have come in about the same time you did.
He came in after me, though.
He came in after you.
Yeah.
Yeah. Well, on that session -- it was a very good session. It was "Ring Dem Bells". Remember?
Yeah. I remember "Ring Dem Bells".
And Sonny calling out in that. That was a good number, wasn't it?
Yeah.
And "Three Little Words" also was a good one.
Yeah.
And then you made "The Mooch", and that featured you.
That featured me. I was using the plunger then.
Yeah. So that was in April. So you joined
the band in November, '29, didn't you?
Yeah. Something like that.
So four months later you were already that familiar with the plunger.
Yeah.
